rv.q: From her very first “loverly”, sheis an irresistible Eliza: radiantly sung, innately funny and thoroughly plausible in a characterisation that avoids cliche on both sides of her “rain in Spain” transformation.
The music, directed and conducted by Oliver Rundell , shimmers, soars and rollicks; Lucy Hind’s choreography, beautifully executed by the cast, gives it crisp physical expression.
Less successful is Madeleine Boyd’s composite set design, with its pub facade and a baffling trapdoor entrance.
The standing ovation was well deserved – this was a superb production.
What a pleasure it is to hear the male quartet in such fine voice in Wouldn’t it be Luverly...
This is a rich, beautiful-looking production, with some wonderful performances; a ‘Loverly’ way to spend 2 hours and 45 minutes.

cn.t: Opera North's My Fair Lady earns near-universal praise, with critics highlighting Katie Bird's irresistible Eliza and sparkling chemistry. A few flag dated gender dynamics, but the lush orchestration and crisp choreography make it a triumphant revival.
